finish_summary: Investigated multiple restructurings of the 32-bit unsigned comparator (balanced binary tree using gt/lt pair propagation, recursive parameterized module, flattened lt/eq propagate tree) to try to reduce area or improve timing slack versus the reference RTL's simple `a < b` operator. estimate_ppa showed none of these alternatives beat the baseline: tree-based versions had equal or higher area and no better (sometimes slightly worse) timing, since Yosys/ABC already optimally maps the built-in comparison operator for this bit width. One recursive-module variant also failed the formal equivalence check due to tool limitations with parameterized recursive instantiation, though functional simulation passed. A place_and_route run on a version with dead code (unused eq_0 wire) removed produced a score statistically indistinguishable from (slightly below) the original baseline, confirming synthesis already prunes such redundancy. Re-running place_and_route on the exact original specification confirmed the best achievable result: area 268.926 um^2, WNS 7.62112 ns, score 75.942274. This is submitted as the final best verified result, as further RTL-level restructuring did not yield measurable improvement and the fixed floorplan/CTS/routing overhead dominates the area budget.
